blocks.text: Billy read Eleanor’s electricity promise twice. Then he laid the newspaper flat on his desk.
“Daniel,” he said.
Jenny stood beside the filing cabinet with her notebook open. “That’s what I thought. She’s paid to keep his laboratory going. Now she has a new energy source she won’t name.”
“He always did like announcing the useful part first.” Billy tapped the page. “Then you found out what he’d done to get it.”
“The lake was supposed to be his good work, too,” Jenny said. “It turned out he was taking power from Perch.”
“And putting it into a robot.”
Jenny came closer to the desk. “But a whole city? The robot was enormous, and that was still only one machine.”
Billy looked toward the electric lamp beside his folders. Beyond the window, buses passed beneath streetlights that would come on after dark.
“He’d need a thousand Super Perches,” Jenny said.
“And the only one we know has left Lake Erie.” Billy pushed the paper away. “Unless he’s found something else.”
Jenny’s fingers stopped on the edge of her notebook.
“Unless…”
Billy looked up.
“Flaming Head.”
The office door opened. Seth came in wearing his red hoodie, with Fist arriving through the window a moment later.
“What about him?” Seth asked.
Jenny showed him the newspaper. “We think Daniel could be behind Eleanor’s electricity plan. We couldn’t see how he’d get enough power.”
Fist hovered over the desk. “He doesn’t have the fish anymore.”
“No,” Jenny said. “But Flaming Head told us his energy was what changed Perch. And Seth. And me.”
Seth looked from her to the paper. “You think Daniel would try to take it from him?”
“He took it from Perch,” Billy said. “We have to consider it.”
Seth pulled out the wooden chair and sat. “Daniel saw him at the robot.”
“So did everybody reading the paper,” Jenny said. “He hasn’t exactly been hiding.”
Fist turned toward the window. “Then let’s go ask the doc what he’s building.”
“I’ll come,” Seth said, rising from the chair. “We know the building.”
Billy raised a hand. “Hold on.”
blocks.alt: In Billy’s Cleveland office, Billy raises a hand to stop civilian Seth from leaving for Daniel’s laboratory. Jenny stands beside the newspaper, and Fist-O-Mite turns back from the open window.

blocks.text: Fist stopped at the sill. “We held on while he built the last one.”
“And I’m not asking you to let him build another,” Billy said. “But you’ve got to play it cool.”
Seth stayed beside the chair. “What if he’s already trying to catch Flaming Head?”

“Then we need to warn him. The police found the old workshop empty. Rushing back there and smashing whatever you find could get you arrested.” Billy looked from Seth to the glove. “Eleanor’s already threatened it. Don’t hand her a reason.”
“He’d be the one doing something wrong,” Seth said.
“If we’re right,” Jenny said. She closed her notebook. “We don’t have proof yet.”
Fist drifted back from the window. “He’ll say it’s research. Everything’s research when somebody catches him.”
“Then we find out what he’s researching,” Billy said. “And we keep our friend out of it.”
Seth looked toward the open window. There was no familiar orange glow outside.
Billy followed his glance. “Have either of you seen Flaming Head today?”
Jenny shook her head. “Not today.”
“Me neither,” Seth said.
Fist’s eyes moved toward the rooftops. “Haven’t seen him.”
For a moment, nobody spoke. Seth reached for the back of the chair again.
“We’re supposed to train with him later today,” he said. “On Jenny’s roof.”
Billy closed his notebook. “Then keep that appointment.”
